drills.stem: You need the minimum equipment grounding conductor (EGC) for a branch circuit protected by a 20A OCPD. What is the correct sizing METHOD?
choices: Size the EGC from Table 250.122 using the rating of the OCPD (20A)
Size the EGC from Table 250.66 using the service-entrance conductor
Match the EGC to the ungrounded conductor's ampacity in Table 310.16
Use the grounding electrode conductor rule in 250.66
hintLadder: Primary noun: equipment grounding conductor (EGC), the wire being sized, not the OCPD or the circuit conductors
Tab family: 250.122 EGC
Cite: Table 250.122, keyed to the OCPD rating. Read the size from your book

drills.stem: Once fall protection is required for a task, which section tells you what makes a guardrail, safety net, or personal fall arrest system COMPLIANT?
choices: 1926.501, the same section that triggers the duty
1926.502, criteria and practices for each system type
1926.503, the training section
1926.1053, since it covers ladder-related fall equipment
hintLadder: Primary noun: SYSTEM criteria, a different question than whether protection is required at all
Tab family: Fall Protection (1926.502)
Cite: 1926.502. Read each system's spec in your book before you pick one

drills.stem: The same circuit is wired with aluminum conductors. Which COLUMN of Table 250.122 applies?
choices: The copper column
The aluminum or copper-clad aluminum column
The OCPD-rating column
Either column, the material does not change the EGC
hintLadder: Primary noun: conductor MATERIAL selects the column, aluminum here
Tab family: 250.122 EGC
Cite: Table 250.122 has separate copper vs aluminum/copper-clad-aluminum columns. Read the aluminum column value in your book

drills.stem: A question asks for the correct setup ANGLE for a non-self-supporting portable ladder. Which section and METHOD do you use?
choices: 1926.1053. Read the exact ratio directly from your book
1926.502, the fall-protection systems section
1926.1060, the training section
Estimate the angle visually. No fixed ratio exists
hintLadder: Primary noun: setup ANGLE, a portable-ladder-specific rule
Tab family: Ladders (1926.1053)
Cite: 1926.1053 states the exact angle ratio. Read it from your book, don't estimate

drills.stem: A question asks where the main bonding jumper connecting the neutral to the enclosure is permitted at service equipment. Which tab family covers that placement rule?
choices: 250.122 EGC (EGC sizing)
250.50 Electrodes (electrode identification)
250 Grounding (GEC sizing at 250.66)
hintLadder: Primary noun: bonding jumper, not the neutral it lands on or the enclosure it lands in
Tab family: 250 Bonding
Cite: 250.28 governs the main bonding jumper. Read the placement rule in your book

drills.stem: An employer assumes verbally reminding employees to 'be careful near the edge' satisfies the fall protection duty. What is actually missing?
choices: Nothing. A verbal reminder satisfies 1926.501 on its own
A protection SYSTEM under 1926.502 plus the training required by 1926.503
Only training under 1926.503. A physical system is never required
Nothing is required until an injury occurs
hintLadder: Primary noun: 'system' and 'training' are two separate requirements once the duty applies
Tab family: Fall Protection (1926.502 systems, 1926.503 training)
Cite: 1926.502 (systems) and 1926.503 (training) both apply once 1926.501 triggers. Confirm both in your book

drills.stem: Ungrounded conductors are upsized from #12 to #8 Cu for voltage drop on a 20A circuit. What must you do for the EGC?
choices: Keep the Table 250.122 size for 20A
Increase the EGC proportionally per 250.122(B) using Chapter 9 Table 8
Always jump to the same size as the ungrounded conductor
The EGC is never increased for voltage drop
hintLadder: Primary noun: equipment grounding conductor + the trigger phrase 'increased in size'
Tab family: 250.122 EGC / 250.122(B)
Cite: 250.122(B). The increase is a circular-mils ratio from Chapter 9 Table 8. Read your book

drills.stem: An employee has used ladders for years without any formal instruction. Does that experience satisfy OSHA's ladder-related training duty?
choices: Yes. Years of informal experience always substitutes for training
No. 1926.1060 requires training on ladder/stairway hazards regardless of tenure
Only if the employee is over a certain age
Only if the ladder is used above a certain height
hintLadder: Primary noun: TRAINING duty, separate from years of informal experience
Tab family: Ladders (1926.1060)
Cite: 1926.1060. The training requirement exists independent of tenure. Confirm the scope in your book

drills.stem: The reduced-size grounding electrode conductor (GEC) allowance applies when the electrode being connected is only of which type?
choices: A concrete-encased electrode
A metal underground water-pipe electrode
A rod, pipe, or plate electrode
Any electrode present at the building
hintLadder: Primary noun: the electrode TYPE that scopes the reduced-size allowance
Tab families: 250 Grounding (the 250.66 allowance) and 250.50 Electrodes (electrode types at 250.52)
Cite: the reduced-size GEC allowance at 250.66 is scoped to rod/pipe/plate electrodes. Reread the exact wording in your book
